title: Salt and Garden
premise: Rafael Blackwood has spent his whole life in the Valley of Stillness, a place where magic cannot cross its borders and where he fled to escape his hedge-witch mistress's increasingly cruel experiments. When he finds tonight's date described in a century-old book of prophecies—along with his own name and the words 'the vessel wakes'—he learns the valley isn't a refuge but a cage, built by his ancestors to contain him: a living vessel for the dormant god of salt. As agents of the Ashen Court close in and the valley's wards begin to fail, Rafael must choose between destroying himself, surrendering to those who would weaponize him, or waking the god on his own terms. In the end, he neither dies nor surrenders—he bargains with the half-awake god, trading his memories of belonging for the valley's freedom, and walks out of the only home he has ever known as a stranger to it.
about_author: Paloma Villalobos is a former botanist who traded field notebooks for fiction after a decade cataloguing endangered coastal plants. She writes fantasy rooted in folk magic, small communities, and the quiet violence of being needed by people who do not see you.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Supposed to Exist
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. On his nineteenth birthday, working in the valley's apothecary, Rafael finds a prophecy book dated 1903 that describes this exact evening—including his name. The emotional beat is vertigo: the safe, dull life he built begins to feel like a stage set.

chapters.title: What the Wards Keep Out
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He tests the valley's border and finds the wards fraying like old rope; beyond them, something tastes his presence. He confides in Marisol, the apothecary's owner, who goes pale and tells him to burn the book. Beat: dread disguised as ordinary kindness.

chapters.title: A Century of Careful Silence
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Flashback chapter revealing that generations of valley keepers have known about 'the vessel'—a child born every few generations carrying the salt god's seed—and were sworn to keep them ignorant and contained. Beat: guilt; Marisol has loved Rafael while lying to him.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Letters
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He decodes letters from Odile, the mistress he fled at fifteen, discovering she didn't lose him—the valley keepers bought him from her, paying her to stay away. Beat: betrayal reframes his entire history of escape.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Sera's POV (introduced). An agent of the Ashen Court crosses the dying wards, tracking the vessel's awakening. She expects a monster and finds a tired young man selling herbs. Beat: unsettling sympathy between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: Tea with the Enemy
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Sera offers Rafael sanctuary with the Court if he comes willingly; Marisol interrupts, and old loyalties collide over a kitchen table. Beat: Rafael realizes everyone wants to decide for him what he is.

chapters.title: The God Under the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Guided by the prophecy book, he descends into the flooded salt mines beneath the valley and hears the god dreaming—a vast, patient loneliness that recognizes him. Beat: terror mixed with terrible kinship.

chapters.title: Everything the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: The god's dream-POV, rendered strange and lyrical. It shows Rafael the ancient war: mages bound it here, and every vessel before him died trying to hold it asleep. Beat: grief across centuries; Rafael understands why the valley was built.

chapters.title: Wards Down
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The wards collapse entirely; the valley's magic-dead stillness begins to invert, and small miracles turn dangerous. The community panics, and suspicion turns on Rafael. Beat: belonging curdling into exile.

chapters.title: The Trial of the Apothecary
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The valley council puts Marisol on trial for harboring the vessel. Rafael confesses publicly to save her—and discovers some neighbors already knew and chose silence out of love. Beat: complicated forgiveness.

chapters.title: Odile Comes Home
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Rafael's former mistress arrives with the Court's second delegation, claiming maternal rights over the vessel. Her tenderness is real and utterly self-serving. Beat: Rafael faces the person who made power look like love.

chapters.title: Two Offers, One Rope
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The Court wants him as a weapon against rival powers; the valley wants him re-bound in deeper sleep; Odile wants him as an heir. All three plans require his consent to work—which is the one thing they can't take. Beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Night of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Ordered to capture Rafael by force, Sera instead burns her writ and warns him, choosing conscience over career. Beat: an alliance built on shared refusal.

chapters.title: Running Out of Valley
chapters.summary: Rafael and Sera flee through the collapsing borderlands while the god's awakening shakes the earth. Rafael's own magic—salt and memory—begins surfacing unbidden. Beat: fugitive intimacy; he stops running and starts choosing.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In an abandoned lighthouse, they find records of a failed fourth path: not sleeping the god, killing it, or serving it—but bargaining. The last vessel left instructions written in her own blood. Beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: Blood Instructions
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Deciphering the dead vessel's notes, he learns the bargain requires payment in memory—everything that makes a place feel like home. Sera begs him not to. Beat: love sharpening the cost.

chapters.title: The Court Arrives
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The full Ashen Court descends on the valley, with Odile at their side, intending to force the awakening under their control. Marisol rallies the valley not to fight but to stand witness. Beat: dread before the storm.

chapters.title: Salt and Garden
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the heart of the salt flats, Rafael wakes the god deliberately—before the Court can seize it—and speaks the bargain: the god may live through him freely if it spares the valley. Beat: the title moment; terror transmuted into agency.

chapters.title: The Price of Walking Away
chapters.summary: The god's and Rafael's braided POV. The payment begins: his mother's kitchen, Marisol's laugh, the smell of the apothecary—all dissolving. He holds on to one memory deliberately and lets the rest go. Beat: sacrifice without martyrdom.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unremembered
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The valley stands, the Court retreats in disarray, and Rafael wakes among people he no longer knows, including a stranger named Sera who cries when he doesn't recognize her. Beat: bittersweet mercy; safety without warmth.

chapters.title: A Stranger Tends the Garden
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Weeks later, Rafael chooses to stay anyway—not because he remembers belonging, but because he decides to build it again from scratch, on his own terms this time. Beat: quiet defiance; belonging as practice, not inheritance.

chapters.title: The Book Rewrites Itself
chapters.summary: Final chapter, omniscient-leaning Rafael POV. In the apothecary, the prophecy book adds new lines in fresh ink—not fate, but invitation. Rafael smiles, picks up a pen, and writes back. Beat: hope; the future as something authored, not foretold.
